newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev stable, c.bank support reported.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev stable, c.bank support reported.

text.p: Dollar sales by the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) offset pressure by the longer value date and stabilised the lev near 224.50 per dollar, the same level as at Wednesday's interbank market close, dealers said.
"Central bank (dollar) sales between 225.50 and 224.50 since opening neutralised downward pressure on the lev due to the longer value date," a bank dealer said.
The value date of today's spot-deals is on Monday and a lev fall to about 230 would be considered normal, the dealer said.
The current large spread between lev-denominated and dollar-denominated deposits allows for a daily lev easing by 1.80-2 levs against the dollar, traders said.
The BNB's main interest rate is now set at an annual 300 percent.
Traders said expectations the International Monetary Fund (IMF) will extend a delayed second $115 million tranche under its funding agreement with Bulgaria also supported the lev.
Local media on Thursday quoted BNB governor Lyubomir Filipov as saying in Washington that Bulgaria now stood a very high chance to receive the tranche. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
